pr_title: Change vertical alignment of scroll target when clicking settings category buttons
pr_body:
Closes #9196
Supersedes #11019  

## Changes

 * Adds test coverage
 * Scroll to 20% lower
   * When scrolled all the way to top is a special case now
   * Manually check if scrolled all the way to bottom because current code doesn't animate the highlighting
 * Consider section intersecting at 25% as selected
   * This is so that scrolling upwards just 1 pixel doesn't instantly unselect the section
 * Prioritize the section user clicked on when scrolled to extremes
   * For this we need to know if the container scrolled to the section or did the user, that's done in ``UserTrackingScrollContainer``
      * Code for this already exists in ``BeatmapCarousel`` so it's extracted from there
pr_comments: I've refactored this to a point I can understand what's going on. Seems to be good enough to get this in.

The "20% lower" figure seems dicey at best seeing that situations like this are apparently possible:

![2021-01-21-233455_1920x1138_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/20418176/105420840-5db98100-5c41-11eb-8aeb-16df1b9d4d2a.png)

The section is pretty much halfway down the scroll - works decent enough for user scrolling, but it's a bit weird when clicking if you ask me. I think `scroll_y_centre = 0.1f` works a bit better but not sure. Feel free to merge past me if you disagree.

Source looks saner to me, so going to dismiss my review on that basis.
Sure let's go with 10%. I think it feels fine (and matches closer to stable, visually).

`public void ScrollTo(Drawable section) =>
            scrollContainer.ScrollTo(scrollContainer.GetChildPosInContent(section) - (FixedHeader?.BoundingBox.Height ?? 0), false);
` 
to disable the animation of the scroll, the problem doesn't occur, implying that somewhere in the scrollTo definition of the framework (probably, I cant find it), UpdateAfterChildren is run before the scroll animation ends, which causes the Update to highlight the section before the correct
